value: In this lesson, we learn two new tricks for reading big words.
But first, let's review some of the letters, sounds, and words we learned in previous lessons.
You know that in little words like ‘he’ and ‘go’, the vowel at the end says its name.
That works INSIDE big words too! When a chunk ends in a vowel, the vowel is ‘open’ — try its name first.
‘Open’ splits into o-pen: the o is open, so it says its name — O-pen!
‘Pilot’ splits into pi-lot: pi . . . lot . . . pilot!
Split each word after the first vowel, let that vowel say its name, then join the chunks.
Sometimes a vowel in a big word is just too sleepy to say its real sound. It mumbles ‘uh’ instead!
Say ‘wagon’. That o isn't saying /o/ OR its name — it's mumbling: wag-uhn.
If you sound out a word carefully and it sounds ALMOST right, try letting a vowel be lazy and mumble ‘uh’.
Read each word. If it sounds almost right, let a vowel go lazy and mumble ‘uh’ — then you'll hear it!

text: Something is hopping along in the wagon.
